name: Conaran

attributes.attribute: often seen as a male prince
spun a web that trapped the heroes

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Conaran is an obscure Irish goddess. She was the mother of three magician daughters. The daughters craved the mighty warriors of the Fianna. They wove a magic net that snared the heroes. The warriors killed all three daughters. Sometimes the tales make Conaran a male figure, a prince of the Tuatha De Danann.

okr.objective: Conaran is an obscure goddess linked to the Fianna.
key_results: Conaran was mother of three magician daughters.
The three cast a web that trapped the Fianna.
The tales also make Conaran a male prince.
